summary: A low level interface that lets a web page drive the graphics processor for drawing and for general computation, designed to map onto the native driver interfaces used on Windows, Apple platforms and Vulkan. It is not finished. Both the main specification and its separate shading language specification are Candidate Recommendation Drafts, both dated 15 September 2026, and the last formally reviewed snapshot of each is 19 December 2024, so no one should cite it as a completed recommendation. What it covers is draw pipelines, compute pipelines, buffers, textures, samplers, command queues, and a system of named optional features and numeric limits that an application must ask for and check. What it leaves to others is everything above that line: no materials, no lighting, no scene tree, no mesh or animation format, no physics, no sound, no networking, no anchors and no input devices. The trap for a spatial computing audience is that this interface cannot yet draw into an immersive session at all, because the binding that would join it to the immersive web interface is an editor's draft that has never been published on the technical reports track, so immersive web content still draws through the older web graphics interface.

coverage.note: Defines render pipelines, render passes, render bundles and command encoders that turn vertex and fragment work into pixels. It has no render graph: the order and structure of passes is the application's business.
